headline: Loss narrows on margin gains, revenue still declines
summary_short: VF Corp's fiscal Q1 2027 (June-quarter) revenue fell 5.2% y/y to $1,669.4M on the Dickies divestiture and weaker Vans wholesale, but gross margin rose 100bps to 54.9% and the net loss narrowed to $(97.2)M ($(0.25)/share) from $(116.4)M a year earlier.
summary_long: Revenue fell 5% y/y on the Dickies divestiture and Active-segment wholesale weakness, partly offset by 5% Outdoor growth (North Face +6%, Timberland +4%) and FX. Gross margin rose 100bps to 54.9% on price increases, lower product costs and mix. SG&A fell $35.5M on lower Reinvent charges and cost savings. Net interest expense fell $16.5M after the February 2026 redemption of €500M of notes. Net loss narrowed to $(97.2)M from $(116.4)M. VF raised FY2027 constant-currency revenue guidance to +2% or better (from +1%-2%); it did not buy back shares and holds $2.5B remaining under its authorization.

drivers.explanation: Net loss narrowed y/y primarily on lower Reinvent transformation-program charges and lower net interest expense, per the filing's own summary of results.
Decrease was primarily due to the Q3 FY2026 Dickies divestiture and lower Active-segment wholesale revenue, partly offset by Outdoor segment growth and favorable FX.

Gross margin (%) rose 100bps on the Dickies divestiture, tactical price increases, lower product costs, mix and lower discounts, partly offset by unfavorable FX; dollar gross profit still fell because revenue fell more than margin expanded.

SG&A fell $35.5M y/y primarily on lower Reinvent restructuring/project costs and Reinvent cost savings, partly offset by higher advertising spend; y/y operating loss narrowed slightly despite lower revenue.

Net interest expense fell $16.5M on the February 2026 early redemption of €500.0M (~$582.2M) of 4.125% senior notes and lower short-term borrowings; effective tax rate was 9.1% vs 8.0% a year earlier.
